analysis:
Reviewed the two supplied head_text units of CHANGELOG.md (lines 747-994 and 995-1220). Both are historical release-note text from v0.9.18 through v0.9.22 (the unchanged tail of the file). The only changed ranges are head lines 11-151, which are outside these units, so I saw only a truncated patch excerpt of the new v0.10.1 candidate section. The section I did see states that the GLM-5.3-Flash logprob groundwork stays disabled and that the release should run behind a coordinator that includes darkbloom-platform#411; I did not verify those claims against source.

The supplied units contain no executable code, configuration, trust-boundary logic, secrets or endpoints. The text describes SSD prefix-cache controls, App Attest, logout and revocation, and fan-helper behavior; these touch T-041, T-053, T-054, TB-011 and TB-010. The text asserts its own limits: source inclusion is not production activation, and candidates are not qualified.

I found no security regression, new attack surface or invalidated threat assumption in these units. No changelog statement contradicts the canonical T-041 posture (30-minute TTL, encrypted SSD, HMAC-keyed names, a cache directory separate from the retired kv root).

Remaining integration question: the actual v0.10.1 changes at lines 11-151 and the code they describe (page-cache memory accounting, the GLM logprob/variable-frame-rate video groundwork, and coordinator-side refusal of logprobs on GLM-5.3-Flash, MiMo V2.6 and Nemotron 3.5 Super) are in other units. The next pass should check those for fail-open behavior, memory admission and DoS (T-010, T-029), and the claim that providers run 0.10.0 behaviour until updated.
